title: Engine tests depend on the host's Reduce Motion setting
description: On Mac Catalyst, UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled reads the host Mac's setting. EngineTests leaves Engine.isReduceMotionEnabled at the real value (the Reduce Motion tests restore it to UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled), so on a CI runner with Reduce Motion on every motion animation snaps: 53 EngineTests failed on PR #7's Catalyst job (and one timed out waiting for an animation that had already finished). Pin Reduce Motion off in every suite that animates, and restore it to off.
acceptance_criteria: Tests pass with the engine's default isReduceMotionEnabled forced to true; Catalyst CI green.
close_reason: Suites pin Reduce Motion off; passes with the engine forced to Reduce Motion on (fails without the fix).

title: Publish 1.1.0 to CocoaPods trunk before it goes read-only
description: kinieta-dg4 decided 1.1.0 is the final CocoaPods release (README/CHANGELOG/podspec summary updated). Trunk permanently stops accepting podspecs on 2 December 2026, with a test shutdown on 1-7 November 2026 (blog.cocoapods.org). Cut 1.1.0: bump s.version in Kinieta.podspec, date the CHANGELOG section, tag 1.1.0, run pod spec lint, then pod trunk push with the maintainer's trunk session. Aim to push before 1 November 2026 to avoid the test window.
notes: Release step for the maintainer: publish after this batch reaches main, before the 1 Nov 2026 trunk test shutdown.

title: Dispatcher runs workers in one shared working tree; they stash and overwrite each other
description: While kinieta-v0k was paused mid-ticket, dispatch.sh deferred it and started kinieta-cxu in the same checkout. The cxu worker stashed v0k's uncommitted changes and later popped them back, so both tickets' edits are now mixed in one tree and either worker could build or commit the other's work. Fix: give each worker its own git worktree (for example herdr --cwd pointing at a fresh 'git worktree add'), or don't defer a ticket whose worker is only waiting for input.
notes:
needs the user's decision on dispatch.sh; keep it out of the automatic worker queue
Resumed 2026-09-28: header of orchestrate.sh already specifies per-ticket worktrees; implementing them in the main loop.
Implemented in commit 95cb9d3 on branch fix/m4z-worker-worktrees (worktree .claude/worktrees/m4z): per-ticket worktrees wt/<ticket> under <repo>-worktrees, ff-merge on close, exit 3 on paused in_progress worker, exit 6 on non-ff. Verified with a stubbed bd/herdr simulation (close, pause+resume, non-ff, dirty tree). Close after it is merged into snapshot-tests.
close_reason: Merged into snapshot-tests (d279d0e): each dispatched worker gets its own git worktree

title: CI silently retries failing tests and runs on an unpinned simulator OS
description:
.github/workflows/ci.yml:
- Line 30: `xcodebuild ... test | xcbeautify ... || xcodebuild ... test`. With pipefail, any failing test makes the first command fail and the whole suite runs again without xcbeautify: flaky tests pass on retry unnoticed and failures take twice as long.
- Line 9: destination 'name=iPhone 17 Pro' has no OS=, so the runtime depends on the runner image. The 72 snapshot references (perceptualPrecision 0.98) were recorded on iOS 26.5; a runner image update can fail them spuriously.
- Line 5: still triggers on the merged 'modernize' branch.
- No concurrency group, so superseded pushes keep running; DerivedData cache key hashes Sources/Tests so it almost never hits exactly.

Slice: install/verify xcbeautify explicitly and drop the retry; pin OS to the recorded runtime (documented next to the snapshots); remove 'modernize'; add concurrency cancel-in-progress; upload .xcresult on failure.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberately failing test fails CI once with readable output; workflow pins the simulator OS; README 'Development' lists the pinned runtime.
close_reason: Retry removed, xcbeautify verified, xcresult uploaded on failure, OS=26.5 + Xcode 26.6 pinned and documented, modernize trigger removed, concurrency added. Tests, example build and lint pass; deliberately failing test fails the step once locally (exit 65).

title: swift build/test fail or are unverified on non-UIKit hosts (macOS, Linux)
description:
README 'Platforms' claims the package 'resolves and builds as an empty module on other platforms'. Nothing verifies that, and the tests are not guarded: EngineTests/ColorTests/SnapshotTests import UIKit unconditionally, so `swift test` from a Mac terminal (the most natural command) fails to compile. Package.swift declares only .iOS(.v17), so on macOS the deployment target defaults to the toolchain minimum, which may be below swift-snapshot-testing's own macOS floor; also check whether consumers resolve swift-snapshot-testing (and its swift-syntax dependency) just by depending on Kinieta.

Slice: wrap the test files in #if canImport(UIKit); add CI jobs for `swift build` + `swift test` on macOS and on Linux (swift:6.x container); fix whatever they surface; record findings about test-only dependency resolution in the ticket and README.
acceptance_criteria: CI has green macOS and Linux build+test jobs; swift test on a Mac runs 0 tests without errors; README statement is verified.
notes: Findings (2026-09-28): (1) Sources were already fully guarded by canImport(UIKit); swift build succeeded on macOS before this change. Only the tests broke swift test (no such module UIKit). Fixed by wrapping all three test files in #if canImport(UIKit). (2) macOS deployment floor: with Package.swift declaring only .iOS(.v17), swift build/test on macOS 26 host (Swift 6.3.3) compiled SnapshotTesting (macOS 10.15 floor) with no errors or warnings; no .macOS platform entry needed. (3) Linux: swift:6.3 container (aarch64) swift build + swift test pass cleanly and run 0 tests. SnapshotTesting and swift-syntax build fine on Linux. (4) Test-only dependency resolution: a scratch consumer depending on Kinieta (file URL, branch snapshot-tests) resolved and checked out only 'kinieta'. swift-snapshot-testing, swift-syntax, swift-custom-dump and xctest-dynamic-overlay are NOT fetched, because SwiftPM target-based resolution prunes deps used only by test targets. Recorded in README Platforms. CI: added spm-macos (macos-26, Xcode 26.6) and spm-linux (container swift:6.3) jobs. Verified locally, not yet on GitHub Actions (branch not pushed).
close_reason: Tests guarded; macOS + Linux swift build/test verified locally (0 tests, no errors); CI jobs added; README verified and extended. iOS tests (57), example build and lint pass.

title: Dynamic colours are resolved against UITraitCollection.current instead of the view's traits
description:
Property.colorLerp (Property.swift:97-140) reads components with getRed/getHue (UIColorExtension.swift:74-87), which resolve dynamic colours with UITraitCollection.current. Inside a CADisplayLink callback that is the app-level fallback, not the animated view's traitCollection. A view with overrideUserInterfaceStyle = .dark in a light app (or a dark sheet over a light screen) interpolates between the light variants and then snaps to the dark target at progress 1. Same for the start colour taken from view.backgroundColor.

The snapshot test dynamicColoursInDarkAppearance renders dark traits only at snapshot time, so the dark 25/50/75 reference PNGs likely encode the light-resolved midpoints.

Slice: resolve source and target with resolvedColor(with: view.traitCollection) before extraction (endpoints still assigned as the original dynamic colours). Unit test with an overridden dark view; re-record and review the dynamic-dark snapshots; demo: add a dark-override swatch in the Colour section.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: view with overrideUserInterfaceStyle = .dark animating .background(.label) has a light (near-white) midpoint; re-recorded dynamic-dark-50 shows a mid-grey between the dark start and white end.
notes: The dynamic-dark snapshot test now sets overrideUserInterfaceStyle on the box itself: a windowless parent's override does not reach subviews, even after updateTraitsIfNeeded. In that test the box starts from .systemPink, not a dark colour, so re-recorded dynamic-dark-50 is a light pink between dark pink and white rather than a mid-grey. The old reference darkened to (121,34,44) and then snapped to white. View.currentTraits calls updateTraitsIfNeeded (iOS 17+) so an override set just before animating is seen.
close_reason: Colours resolve against view.traitCollection; unit test, re-recorded dark snapshots, demo swatch. Tests (97), example build and lint pass.

title: Paused timelines keep the display link running at 120 Hz forever
description:
Engine keeps every registered action in `actions` (Engine.swift:114) and only stops the CADisplayLink when that list is empty (Engine.swift:145-147). A paused SequenceAction returns .running every frame (Sequence.swift:28), so while any handle is paused the display link fires at the preferred 120 Hz doing nothing. If the app pauses a handle and then drops it (discardableResult), the display link never stops for the life of the process: a battery drain with no way to recover. wait(.infinity) has the same effect.

Slice: let actions report 'idle' (paused) and have Engine pause the driver when every action is idle, resuming on resume()/add(). Tests with the manual driver asserting the driver is stopped/paused. Note in README 'Frame rate'.
acceptance_criteria: Test: after pausing the only running handle the driver reports not running; resume() restarts it and the animation continues from where it was.
close_reason: Engine stops the driver when every action is idle (paused or wait(.infinity)); resume/cancel/add restart it. Tests, example build and lint pass.

title: Appending to a handle after its timeline started or finished is silently lost (builder and runtime share one queue)
description:
Kinieta registers mainSequence with the engine in init (Kinieta.swift:46-51) and the builder methods mutate that live queue.
- let h = view.animate(.x(1), duration: 0.1); later h.animate(.x(2), duration: 1): if the first part finished, mainSequence was removed from the engine and state is .finished, so the new action never runs and nothing reports it.
- The public Kinieta(for:) (Kinieta.swift:42) promises 'an empty timeline', but an empty timeline completes on the very next frame, so a handle built in a later run-loop turn is dead.
- repeat(times:) copies mainSequence.types, which no longer contains the action currently running, so repeat after the first frame drops it.
- easing/onComplete after start may target the wrong action.

Architecture: separate the immutable timeline description (builder) from the running instance. Decide the contract (recommend: appending to a finished handle re-arms it: state back to .running, re-register with engine; repeat copies the full description regardless of progress).

Slice: implement contract; tests via manual frame driver for append-after-finish, Kinieta(for:) built one frame later, repeat after start; README/DocC wording.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: appended animation after finish runs and finished() awaits it; Kinieta(for:) handle built after one frame still animates; repeat(times: 1) after the first frame plays the whole chain twice.
close_reason: Handle keeps its timeline description apart from the running sequence. Adding to a finished handle restarts it (grouped members rejoin a running group); repeat copies the whole chain; modifiers only reach unstarted actions; finished timelines release their blocks. Tests, example build and lint pass.

title: Kinieta.group: cancelling the group strands child handles; a handle grouped twice runs at double speed
description:
Kinieta.group (Kinieta.swift:210-216) removes each child's mainSequence from the engine and drives them from a Group owned by a new handle. There is no ownership model:
1. groupHandle.cancel() cancels only the group's own sequence. Children are no longer updated by anyone, keep state == .running forever, and any `await child.finished()` never returns (leaked continuation).
2. groupHandle.pause()/resume() works, but children still report isRunning == true.
3. Kinieta.group(a, a), or putting one handle into two groups, updates the same Sequence twice per frame, so it animates at 2x (or more) speed.
4. Grouping a handle that has already finished re-runs its completion (Sequence with empty queue calls complete again).
5. Removing the children from the engine can momentarily empty it, stopping the display link and restarting it with a reset clock.

Slice: give SequenceAction an owner (engine or one group) and reject/ignore a second owner (debug warning); dedupe handles; propagate cancel/pause/resume from the group handle to its children's state (children become .cancelled with waiters resumed); skip already-terminal handles. Tests through the manual frame driver. Document the semantics in README 'Grouping views'.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: cancel group → every child state .cancelled and child finished() returns; group(a, a) moves a at 1x; grouping a finished handle does not re-fire its completion; paused group reports children paused.
close_reason: Group owns members: cancel/pause/resume propagate, duplicates/owned/ended handles left out, engine never empties. Tests, example build, lint pass.

title: cancel()/pause() called from a completion block does not stop the timeline in that frame; .cancelled is overwritten by .finished
description:
Sequence.update (Sequence.swift:26-52) checks isCancelled/isPaused only on entry. Scenario:

  let h = view.animate(.x(100), duration: 1).onComplete { h.cancel() }
             .animate(.alpha(0))             // zero duration

When the first animation completes mid-frame, its block calls h.cancel() (Kinieta.swift:173): isCancelled = true, state = .cancelled, waiters resumed. Control returns into the while loop, which pops the next action and runs it with the leftover overshoot: alpha is set to 0 and its completion fires despite the cancel. If the queue is then empty, `complete?()` runs finish(as: .finished) and the public state flips from .cancelled to .finished. pause() from a completion block has the same leak for one frame.

Slice: re-check isCancelled/isPaused inside the loop after every child update; make Kinieta.finish idempotent (first terminal state wins). Tests through the public handle using the manual frame driver. Note the guarantee in the 'Controlling a timeline' README section.
acceptance_criteria: Test: cancel inside onComplete leaves alpha untouched, fires no later completion, state stays .cancelled; pause inside onComplete holds the next action at progress 0.
close_reason: Main sequence re-checks cancel/pause after each child; finish is idempotent. Tests, example build, lint pass. Nested-sequence leak filed as kinieta-2e7.

title: Easing.inOut(.sine) is identical to .inOut(.quad)
description:
Easing.swift:56 and :60 both return Bezier(0.455, 0.03, 0.515, 0.955). That is Ceaser's easeInOutQuad; easeInOutSine is Bezier(0.445, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95) (easings.net today lists cubic-bezier(0.37, 0, 0.63, 1)). Every other preset matches the Ceaser table. The demo shows the 'inOut(.sine)' and 'inOut(.quad)' tracks moving identically.

The existing test everyPresetResolvesForEveryPlacement only checks in != out, so the duplicate slipped through.

Slice: fix the constant (pick one source and note it in the header comment at Easing.swift:2); add a test that all 21 preset Béziers are pairwise distinct and a reference-function check for sineInOut (0.5 - cos(pi t)/2) in presetCurvesApproximateEasingsNetReferenceFunctions; confirm visually in the demo; CHANGELOG 'Fixed'.
acceptance_criteria: New distinctness test fails before the fix and passes after; sineInOut is within 0.06 of the closed form at t = 0.25/0.5/0.75; demo tracks for sine and quad differ.
close_reason: inOut(.sine) now uses Ceaser easeInOutSine (0.445, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95); added pairwise-distinctness test (failed before fix on sine/quad inOut only) and sineInOut/quadInOut reference checks; demo tracks verified to differ; CHANGELOG Fixed entry. Tests (61), demo build and lint pass.

title: Negative, NaN and infinite durations break timelines (fast-forward or hang forever)
description:
Pause.swift:19-25: `elapsed >= duration` then returns `.finished(overshoot: elapsed - duration)`.
- wait(-5) / delay(-5): overshoot = dt + 5, so Sequence (Sequence.swift:40-49) hands a 5-second frame to the next action, which jumps straight to its end state.
- wait(.nan): `elapsed >= .nan` is always false, so the timeline never finishes, finished() never returns, and the display link runs forever.
- animate(duration: .nan) snaps (guard duration > 0 fails), inconsistent with wait.
- wait(.infinity) / animate(duration: .infinity) never finish; decide whether that is supported.
- repeat(times:) already clamps negatives; nothing else validates input.

Slice: define the contract (recommend: negative and NaN treated as 0 with a debug warning; infinity allowed only for wait, documented). Sanitise in one place (the Kinieta builder), cap overshoot at frame.duration in PauseAction. Tests for each input via synthetic frames. README/DocC note under Sequencing.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: wait(-5) followed by a 1 s animation is at ~50% after 0.5 s; wait(.nan) finishes within one frame; behaviour documented.
close_reason: Negative/NaN durations sanitised to 0 with a warning in the Kinieta builder; infinity allowed for wait/delay only; PauseAction overshoot capped at the frame. Tests, example build and lint pass.

title: Prefactor: injectable frame driver for Engine so end-to-end tests are deterministic
description:
Why: Engine (Sources/Kinieta/Engine.swift:110-155) is a singleton hard-wired to CADisplayLink. The end-to-end tests (EngineTests.swift:545-627) rely on Task.sleep and wall-clock timing, e.g. cancelStopsTheTimelineWhereItIs expects 0 < x < 100 after sleeping 150 ms, which is flaky on loaded CI runners. Many lifecycle bugs filed alongside this ticket need to be reproduced through the public Kinieta handle API, which requires stepping the engine by hand.

Slice:
1. Introduce an internal `FrameDriver` protocol (start(onFrame:), stop()) with the CADisplayLink implementation (current Engine.DisplayLink) and a `ManualFrameDriver` for tests that exposes `step(_ dt:)`.
2. Let tests swap the driver on Engine.shared (internal setter or init injection) and restore it afterwards.
3. Remove dead code: Engine.DisplayLink.pause()/resume() (Engine.swift:79-85) are never called. Frame.timestamp is only passed through; keep or drop deliberately.
4. Rewrite the six display-link tests to step frames deterministically; keep one smoke test on the real CADisplayLink.
5. Document the test helper in EngineTests.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests contain no Task.sleep; the suite passes 20 consecutive runs locally (xcodebuild test -test-iterations 20 or equivalent loop); a single real-display-link smoke test remains.
notes: Added internal FrameDriver protocol (Engine.swift); Engine.DisplayLink renamed DisplayLinkDriver; dead pause()/resume() removed. Engine.driver is an internal var: swapping stops the old driver and starts the new one if actions are registered. Frame.timestamp dropped deliberately (only SequenceAction passed it through); Frame is now Frame(duration). ManualFrameDriver lives in Tests/KinietaTests (install()/uninstall()/step(_:count:)). Six end-to-end tests rewritten on the manual driver, no Task.sleep; one real-CADisplayLink smoke test kept (realDisplayLinkRunsATimelineToCompletion); 2 new driver lifecycle tests. 60/60 pass; -test-iterations 20 all green; demo builds; lint --strict clean.
close_reason: Injectable FrameDriver + ManualFrameDriver; end-to-end tests deterministic with no Task.sleep; one real display-link smoke test remains; 20 consecutive iterations pass; demo build and strict lint pass.

title: Prefactor: rename internal action types and give ActionType named payloads
description:
Why: several later tickets touch the action tree; do this rename first so they build on legible code.

Problems:
- Sources/Kinieta/Sequence.swift:8 declares `final class Sequence`, which shadows Swift.Sequence everywhere in the module (and in @testable test targets). `Group` and `Animation` collide with SwiftUI.Group/SwiftUI.Animation, which blocks adding the planned SwiftUI bridge inside the module.
- Action.swift:40 `ActionType` uses positional associated values: `.animation(ViewRef, [Property], TimeInterval, Bezier?, Block?)`. Kinieta.swift:122-133 (applying easing) and :154-167 (onComplete) destructure and rebuild it by position, duplicating logic.
- Property.swift:34 dedupes by a stringly-typed `name`.
- Group.swift:11 models state as `running: [Action]?` where nil means 'not started' and [] means 'done'; two initialisers with different semantics. ActionQueue is a base class shared by inheritance.

Slice:
1. Rename Sequence→SequenceAction, Group→GroupAction, Animation→PropertyAnimation, Pause→PauseAction (internal only; no public API change).
2. Replace positional payloads with small structs (e.g. AnimationSpec {view, properties, duration, easing, completion}) plus helpers `withEasing(_:)` / `withCompletion(_:)` on ActionType so Kinieta.easing/onComplete become one-liners.
3. Replace `Property.name: String` with `Property.Key` enum (keep `description` for ActionType.description).
4. Make GroupAction's lifecycle explicit (enum state) and prefer composition over ActionQueue inheritance if it reads better.
5. Update tests (EngineTests uses Sequence/Group/Animation/Pause directly).
Pure refactor: no behaviour change, snapshots untouched.
acceptance_criteria: All 57 tests pass unchanged in behaviour; no type named Sequence/Group/Animation/Pause remains in Sources; swift-format lint --strict passes; public API diff is empty.
close_reason: Renamed action types (SequenceAction, GroupAction, PropertyAnimation, PauseAction), AnimationSpec + labelled payloads with withEasing/withCompletion, Property.Key enum, GroupAction explicit Phase, ActionQueue now a struct owned by SequenceAction. 57/57 tests pass on iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.5 with no snapshot re-record; swift-format lint --strict clean; demo builds; public API unchanged.

title: Rewrite the orchestrator in Go with a Bubble Tea UI
description: Port .claude/orchestrate.sh to Go (own repo ~/Projects/orchestrate) with the same behaviour, env vars, log file and exit codes, plus a Bubble Tea terminal UI: each dispatched ticket shown with its title, each completed ticket shown (ID only) in a distinct colour, and a live status line for the current worker.
acceptance_criteria: Same exit codes and log format as the bash script; picked-up tickets print ID + title; completed tickets print ID only in a different colour; live status for the current worker; plain output when not on a TTY; unit tests for parsing and decisions pass.
notes: Built in ~/Projects/orchestrate (not committed yet). Unit tests pass; verified in a Herdr pane on a demo repo: setup checks, empty queue, deferred path, and a full dispatch -> worker -> close -> merge -> cleanup run. Fixed vs bash: agent start retry into an occupied pane (START_FAILED).

title: Decide whether the next release is pushed to CocoaPods trunk
description: kinieta-2wu fixed the podspec (privacy manifest, description) on main, but 1.0.0 on trunk still lacks the privacy manifest, and README/CHANGELOG call 1.0.0 the final CocoaPods release. Decide: (a) push the next release (1.1.0, given Unreleased has Added entries) to trunk and update the README 'final CocoaPods release' line, (b) cut a podspec-only 1.0.1 from tag 1.0.0, or (c) leave trunk at 1.0.0 and accept CocoaPods consumers lack the manifest.
notes: Decision (maintainer): option (a). 1.1.0 is pushed to CocoaPods trunk as the final CocoaPods release; no podspec-only 1.0.1. title: Run the full CI suite locally from one script; workers gate on it
description: The worker prompt runs only 3 of the 6 CI jobs (iOS test + example build, lint), so Catalyst, tvOS, SwiftPM-macOS and SwiftPM-Linux failures surface only after a push, and the prompt tells workers to defer anything that needs CI. Add scripts/ci-local.sh running all six checks (Linux via Docker swift:6.3 with --scratch-path .build-linux), stopping at the first failure. Rewrite the worker prompt to use it and merge its two sets of close rules into one; the awaits-CI deferral remains only for tickets that change .github/workflows/.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/ci-local.sh runs the five local checks (lint, spm-macos, ios, catalyst, spm-linux; tvOS is CI only by decision) and passes on main; a single named check can be run on its own; worker prompt has one set of close rules gated on the script; workers are allowed to run it without a permission prompt.
notes:
Verified on main (Xcode 26.6): lint, spm-macos (0 tests, by design), ios (129 tests), catalyst (124 tests), spm-linux pass. tvos not run: the tvOS platform is not installed on this Mac; the script reports that as a setup problem (exit 2) with the install command. Not committed yet (branch ci-local).
tvOS dropped from the local script at the user's request; the CI tvos job stays. Full local run: 5/5 pass in 34s.
close_reason: scripts/ci-local.sh runs the five local checks (tvOS is CI only); worker prompt gates on it. 5/5 pass on ci-local.

title: cancel()/pause() from a completion block still leaks inside nested sequences (then, delay) and groups
description: kinieta-e9c made the main SequenceAction re-check isCancelled/isPaused after every child update, but only the main sequence carries those flags. Nested SequenceActions built by then (.group([.sequence(...)])) and delay, and GroupAction children, keep running in the same frame. Example: let h = view.animate(.x(100), duration: 1); h.onComplete { h.cancel() }.animate(.alpha(0)).then — the inner sequence runs alpha(0) with the leftover overshoot before the main sequence sees the cancel. The state stays .cancelled now (finish is idempotent), but the view is still mutated and inner completions fire. Fix idea: have nested actions consult the owning timeline's stop/pause state, e.g. a shared token passed down through makeAction.
close_reason: Nested sequences and groups share the timeline's TimelineControl and stop after any child when it is cancelled/paused. 7 new tests (fail before the fix). Full scripts/ci-local.sh passes. No dependents. View-loss analogue filed as kinieta-6yl.

title: CocoaPods podspec ships without the privacy manifest and with a stale description
description:
Kinieta.podspec:30 only lists source_files; PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy (shipped to SwiftPM consumers via Package.swift:19) is not included, so CocoaPods consumers get no privacy manifest for the SDK. The description (Kinieta.podspec:7-17) still says 'A library written in Swift 4.0' and has typos ('requiremenets where').

Slice: add s.resource_bundles = { 'Kinieta_Privacy' => ['Sources/Kinieta/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy'] }; rewrite the description from README; pod lib lint --allow-warnings in CI (optional job). Since 1.0.0 is the declared final CocoaPods release, decide whether this ships as 1.0.1 and note it in CHANGELOG.
acceptance_criteria: pod lib lint passes; the built pod contains the privacy bundle; description matches README.
close_reason: Podspec ships PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in a Kinieta_Privacy resource bundle; description matches README. pod lib lint --platforms=ios passes (tvOS lint not possible locally: no tvOS simulator); bundle verified in the built app. Not a 1.0.1 — noted in CHANGELOG. Full scripts/ci-local.sh passed. Follow-ups filed: optional CI pod lint job, trunk release decision.

title: Public namespace hygiene: generic Block typealias and module named like its main class
description:
1. Action.swift:29 `public typealias Block = () -> Void` exports a very generic name into every consumer's namespace; it is also not @MainActor although it is always called on the main actor.
2. The module Kinieta exports a class Kinieta. Consumers who have their own Property/Easing/Engine type cannot write Kinieta.Property to disambiguate, because Kinieta resolves to the class. This is also the known cause of broken .swiftinterface files under BUILD_LIBRARY_FOR_DISTRIBUTION (XCFramework distribution).
3. Property, Engine, Easing, Bezier are generic top-level names.

Slice (non-breaking for 1.x): add nested typealiases on the class (Kinieta.Property, Kinieta.Easing, Kinieta.Completion = @MainActor () -> Void) so disambiguation works; deprecate the top-level Block; add a test target file that declares its own Property type and uses Kinieta.Property; try building with BUILD_LIBRARY_FOR_DISTRIBUTION=YES in CI and record the result; plan the 2.0 rename in CHANGELOG.
acceptance_criteria: A test file with a local 'struct Property' compiles using Kinieta.Property; Block is deprecated; library-evolution build result documented (and green if achievable).
notes:
Done in 2d90e35 on wt/kinieta-6zf; full scripts/ci-local.sh passes (lint, spm-macos, ios 196 tests, catalyst 190, evolution, spm-linux); docbuild has no warnings. AWAITS CI: adds an 'evolution' job to .github/workflows/ci.yml.
- Kinieta.Property/CustomProperty/Interpolatable/Easing/Bezier/ColorInterpolation/Engine/ReduceMotionBehavior nested aliases (Sources/Kinieta/Namespace.swift). They go through doc-hidden public _Kinieta* aliases: inside the class the bare name is the alias itself, and Kinieta::Property (module selectors) needs Swift 6.3 while Package.swift declares tools 6.0.

description:

title: await handle.finished() ignores Task cancellation
description:
Kinieta.finished() (Kinieta.swift:193-196) uses withCheckedContinuation with no cancellation handler. A Task awaiting a long or paused timeline (e.g. a SwiftUI .task or a view model that is torn down) stays suspended until the timeline ends, which for a paused or wait(.infinity) timeline is never; the continuation and everything the task captured leak.

Slice: wrap in withTaskCancellationHandler; on cancellation remove that waiter and return (do not cancel the animation; document it; optionally offer finished(cancellingOnTaskCancel:)). Tests with the manual driver and Task.cancel().
acceptance_criteria: Test: cancelling a Task awaiting a paused handle returns promptly; the handle stays paused; other waiters are unaffected.
close_reason: finished() uses withTaskCancellationHandler; cancelled waiter is removed and resumed, timeline untouched. Tests, example build, lint pass.

title: When the view is deallocated mid-timeline, remaining pauses and completions still run and the handle reports .finished
description:
Only PropertyAnimation checks the weak view (Animation.swift:40); it finishes without calling its completion. The rest of the timeline keeps going: a following wait(10) holds the sequence (and the display link) for 10 s, pause completion blocks and the timeline completion still fire, and the handle ends as .finished. README says 'A timeline finishes on its own when its view is deallocated', which is only true for animation-only timelines. Completion semantics are inconsistent: the animation's block is skipped, later blocks run.

Slice: when a handle that had a view loses it, end the whole timeline promptly with a defined terminal state (recommend .cancelled, no further completions; group handles, which have no view, are exempt). Tests through the manual frame driver; README/DocC wording.
acceptance_criteria: Test: view released during animate(...).wait(10).onComplete{} ends the handle within one frame, the wait's completion does not fire, state matches the documented one.
close_reason: View loss now cancels the whole timeline within one frame; tests, example build and lint pass. Follow-up for idle timelines: kinieta-nlf

title: Colours that cannot convert to RGB are treated as transparent; LCH achromatic threshold uses the wrong scale
description:
1. UIColorExtension.swift:82-87 ignores the Bool returned by getRed. Pattern colours (UIColor(patternImage:)) and some CGColors (layer.borderColor in a CMYK or generic colour space, via UIColor(cgColor:) at View.swift:75) return false with all zeros, so colorLerp sees alpha 0 and treats the endpoint as clear: the animation fades instead of blending, silently.
2. Property.swift:130-132 treats LCH chroma < 1e-3 as achromatic, but LCH chroma is on a 0–~130 scale (the HSB branch uses the same 1e-3 on 0–1). Near-greys such as .systemGray (chroma ≈ 3) keep a noisy hue and sweep through unrelated hues when blended to a saturated colour.

Slice: convert via CGColor.converted(to: extendedSRGB) and fall back to snapping (with a debug warning) when conversion is impossible; scale the achromatic threshold per space (e.g. chroma < 2 for LCH) or weight hue by chroma. Tests: pattern colour endpoint, CMYK CGColor border, .systemGray→.systemBlue hue stays near blue.
acceptance_criteria: Tests above pass; no change to existing colour snapshots except where the hue-sweep fix is intended (review any re-recorded PNG).
close_reason: Pattern colours now snap at animation start with a logged warning instead of fading as transparent. LCH hue is weighted by squared chroma below 20, so near-greys head straight for the target hue. Premise check: on iOS 26.5 getRed converts DeviceCMYK, generic CMYK, Lab, XYZ and grey CGColors itself, so the CGColor.converted fallback would be dead code and was left out; a CMYK border test guards the behaviour. .systemGray is bluish (hue 290 vs .systemBlue 287), so its test also runs a warm near-grey that fails on the old code. Re-recorded dynamic-{light,dark}-{25,50,75}: the teal border no longer sweeps through lavender to .secondaryLabel. Tests (117), example build and lint pass. Commit 033f6de.

title: Rotation start value wraps to (-180°, 180°] and discards any scale in the transform
description:
View.swift:65-68 reads rotation as atan2(transform.b, transform.a) and writes a pure rotation transform.
- animate(.rotation(degrees: 270)) then animate(.rotation(degrees: 360)): the second starts from -90 and spins 450° instead of 90°.
- Multi-turn rotations cannot be continued: after .rotation(degrees: 720) the next animation starts from 0.
- Any existing scale/translation in view.transform is discarded on the first frame (documented as 'replaces any scale', but surprising and not fixable by the user).

Slice: keep a logical rotation per view (associated object or a side table keyed by ObjectIdentifier) used as the start value, and decompose the current transform so scale/translation are preserved when composing the rotation. Tests for 270→360 (90° travel), 720 then 810, and preserved scale. Update README property table ('replaces any scale').
acceptance_criteria: Tests: 270→360 rotates through 90° only; a view with scale 2 keeps scale 2 after a rotation animation; demo easing tracks still reset correctly.
close_reason: Logical per-view rotation (associated object) used as the start value while the transform is unchanged; rotation composed onto existing scale/translation. Tests for 270→360, 720→810, preserved scale, external reset. README updated. Tests, demo build, lint pass.

title: The .frame property is undefined on rotated views and is not clamped under overshooting easing
description:
Property.swift:67-68 interpolates view.frame directly. UIKit documents frame as undefined when transform is not identity, so .frame combined with .rotation (or on an already rotated view) sends the view to the wrong place, while .x/.y/.width/.height were deliberately routed through center/bounds (View.swift:29-63) to avoid exactly that. .width/.height/.borderWidth/.cornerRadius are clamped at 0 but .frame is not: with .inOut(.back) shrinking to a small rect the width goes negative and UIKit standardises the rect, so the view jumps.

Slice: implement .frame via the x/y/width/height helpers with the size clamp; tests on a rotated view and with backInOut; add a rotated-frame snapshot; README property table note.
acceptance_criteria: Test: .frame target on a view rotated 45° ends with center/bounds matching the target rect; backInOut to a 2x2 rect never produces negative bounds.
close_reason: The .frame property now goes through center/bounds (UIView.untransformedFrame) with the size clamped at 0 and the target standardised. Added tests for a view rotated 45°, for backInOut to 2x2, and for a negative-size target, plus the rotated-frame snapshots and a README note. Tests, the example build and the lint all pass.

title: Chain calls on a Kinieta.group handle are silently dropped
description:
Kinieta.group stores the Group in mainSequence.currentAction and leaves mainSequence.types empty (Kinieta.swift:213-214). Consequently on the returned handle:
- .onComplete { } → popLast() returns nil → dropped (Kinieta.swift:155). Users naturally write Kinieta.group(a, b).onComplete { } instead of the completion: parameter.
- .easing/.delay → dropped.
- .repeat(times:) → copies nothing.
- .animate(...) → handle.view is nil, so the animation targets ViewRef(nil) and finishes instantly without running.

Slice: represent the group as an ordinary queued action (so onComplete/delay/repeat/wait-after work), and make animate on a view-less handle a documented precondition/diagnostic. Tests for onComplete, delay and wait-then-continue on a group handle. README example of group(...).onComplete.
acceptance_criteria: Kinieta.group(a, b).onComplete { } fires once after both finish; .delay(0.5) postpones the group; .wait(1).onComplete {} chains after the group.
notes: Committed as bea8a68 (the close reason names be9ac93, the hash before an amend).
close_reason: Group is now a queued .timelines step; onComplete/delay/wait/repeat work on group handles; animate on a group handle is ignored with a warning. Tests (102), example build and lint pass. Commit be9ac93 (amended).

title: Prefactor: consolidate colour conversion into one internal module; deprecate leaked HandyUIKit UIColor API
description:
Why: colour code is split across three files with overlapping models, and a vendored helper leaks public API into every consumer.

Problems:
- UIColorExtension.swift (vendored from HandyUIKit) makes public: `ChangeableColorComponent`, `UIColor.change(_:by:)`, `UIColor.change(_:to:)`, `hlca`, `hsba`, `rgba`, `UIColor(hue:luminance:chroma:alpha:)`. None are needed by consumers of an animation library; apps that also use HandyUIKit get ambiguity errors. `change(.alpha, to:)` round-trips through LCH without clamping, so changing alpha also shifts the colour.
- UIColor+Components.swift:34 `public struct Components` has only internal members and init, so it is public but unusable; its +/- operators fatalError on mismatched spaces.
- ColorSpaces.swift: `RGBColor.sRGBCompand` actually linearises (inverse companding) while `XYZColor.sRGBCompand` compands; constants use rounded CIE values (LAB_K_116 = 7.787036, LAB_E = 0.008856) instead of the exact 24389/27/116 and 216/24389; `LCHColor.MaxL/MaxC/MaxH` break naming style.
- Three representations (Components, RGBColor/LCHColor, UIColor tuples) for the same thing.

Slice:
1. One internal `ColorMath` (or similar) file: sRGB⇄linear⇄XYZ⇄Lab⇄LCH with clear names and exact constants, plus a single `extractComponents(of:)` entry point that Property.colorLerp uses.
2. Mark the HandyUIKit extensions and UIColor.Components `@available(*, deprecated, message: ...)` for 1.x (1.0.0 is tagged, so removal waits for 2.0); stop using them internally.
3. Keep ColorTests reference values; add a round-trip test for the new module.
4. CHANGELOG 'Deprecated' entry; DocC migration note.
acceptance_criteria: Property.colorLerp uses only the new internal module; deprecated symbols compile with warnings for consumers; ColorTests and all colour snapshots pass without re-recording.
close_reason: ColorMath.swift replaces ColorSpaces.swift with exact CIE constants; Property.colorLerp uses only ColorMath.extractComponents(of:); HandyUIKit helpers and UIColor.Components deprecated (consumer warnings verified); CHANGELOG Deprecated entry + DocC DeprecatedColorHelpers article. 96 tests pass, snapshots unchanged, example builds, lint clean. Commit 2961fe7.

title: Add a way to repeat a timeline until it is cancelled
description:
There is no way to loop an animation until it is cancelled, which is what a spinner, a pulsing badge or a breathing placeholder needs. repeat(times:) (Kinieta.swift:270) only appends a fixed number of copies, and it builds them all at once: repeat(times: .max), the obvious guess for "forever", loops Int.max times on the main thread and hangs the app.

The workarounds today are awkward: re-extend the handle from its own onComplete (the block has to capture the handle, and the cycle is only broken by cancel()), or run `while !Task.isCancelled { await view.animate(...).finished() }`, which makes a new handle every cycle, so there is no single handle to pause or cancel.

UIKit (UIView.AnimationOptions.repeat), Core Animation (repeatCount = .infinity) and SwiftUI (repeatForever) all offer this, so users will look for it.
design:
Suggested spelling: repeatForever(), next to repeat(times:), with the same meaning: replay the whole chain so far, including actions that are already running or done, until cancel(). Leave repeat(times:) semantics unchanged.

Points to settle:
- Represent the loop as a single queue step that replays its steps (for example ActionType.loop), not as copies, so memory stays flat.
- Actions added after repeatForever() can never run: warn in debug builds through Kinieta.ignored, as other no-op chain calls do.
- finished() returns only on cancel, or when the view is released. On a group handle the group completion never fires. onComplete blocks inside the chain fire on every cycle, as they do for repeat(times:) copies.
- A cycle that takes no time must not spin inside one frame: all durations zero, or every property snapping under Reduce Motion. Advance at most one cycle per frame.
- pause()/resume(), interruption by a newer animation on the same property, and group membership should behave as they do for any other timeline.
- Consider rejecting or capping a huge repeat(times:) with a warning, pointing to repeatForever().
acceptance_criteria: repeatForever() loops a chain until cancel(), holding a constant number of queued steps; finished() returns on cancel; a zero-duration or Reduce-Motion-snapped cycle advances once per frame instead of hanging; a debug warning for calls chained after it; tests driven by ManualFrameDriver; README (Chaining, Troubleshooting table), DocC and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] updated; demo shows a looping animation.
close_reason: repeatForever() added (one loop step, at most one cycle start per frame, debug warning for calls after it), repeat(times:) capped at 10,000; tests in RepeatForeverTests; README, DocC, CHANGELOG, both demos updated. Full scripts/ci-local.sh and DocC (iOS, macOS) pass. Commit 21fcbcd.

Fix: let a .custom property whose key path writes the view's transform claim .rotation as well (and .rotation claim that key path), keeping in mind that key paths rooted in subclasses (\UIImageView.transform) hash differently from \UIView.transform.

title: A member of a dropped paused group can never run again
description: If a Kinieta.group handle is paused (which pauses its members) and then released while a member handle is kept, member.resume() succeeds (its weak owner is now nil) and the member reports .running, but its sequence is only driven by the group's GroupAction, whose sequence stays paused forever. The member never advances and its finished() never returns; only cancel() ends it. Before kinieta-0pl the paused group sequence sat in Engine.actions forever; now the engine drops it as abandoned, with the same outcome for the member. Options: when a group handle deinits, hand its unfinished members back to the engine (clearing owner), or refuse resume() on a member whose group went away paused.
close_reason: Chose option 1: a paused group handle's deinit hands the members its GroupAction still runs to the engine, keeping their state (skipped if a member has since joined another group or ended). Tests cover resume after release, a member adopted while paused, a member regrouped before the hand-over, and a released running group. Full scripts/ci-local.sh passes. Commit 82c12e9.

title: Test suites that change Engine.shared settings can run in parallel

EngineTests and CustomPropertyTests set Engine.shared.isReduceMotionEnabled = { true } and colorInterpolation = .rgb inside some tests, so a test in another suite running at the same moment can see those values and snap or interpolate differently. No failure seen yet. Fix: run every suite that touches Engine.shared serially, e.g. nest them in one parent @Suite(.serialized), or inject the settings instead of mutating the shared engine.
acceptance_criteria: No suite can observe another suite's temporary Engine.shared settings; full test run passes repeatedly.

title: Interpolatable conformances for CGAffineTransform and CGColor

Its motivation listed transform scale, but CGAffineTransform is not Interpolatable: a component-wise lerp is wrong for rotation, so it needs decomposition into translation, rotation (shorter arc or unwrapped, matching .rotation) and scale/shear, like Core Animation. CGColor (layer.shadowColor, a CGColor?) has no conformance either; it could reuse ColorMath.interpolator through UIColor(cgColor:). Add both, with tests, and a README row; consider whether .custom(\.transform) should default isMotion to true.

title: Releasing the view from a completion block inside then/delay/parallel still runs the rest of that nested step
description: kinieta-2e7 made nested sequences and groups honour cancel()/pause() through a shared TimelineControl, but the view-lost check (SequenceAction.cancelIfViewIsGone) still runs only in the main sequence, which carries the target. Example: view.wait(1).onComplete { container = nil /* releases view */ }.wait(0).onComplete { fires }.then — the inner sequence runs wait(0) and its completion in the same frame before the main sequence notices the view is gone. Animations on a nil view are harmless, but pause/sequence/group completions still fire. Fix idea: move target/onViewLost onto TimelineControl so every nested sequence and group checks it after each child, as they do for isCancelled.

title: A paused or wait(.infinity) timeline is not cancelled when its view is released while the engine is idle
description: kinieta-6v7 cancels a timeline whose view is gone, but the check runs in SequenceAction.update. When every timeline is idle (paused, or waiting forever) the engine stops its driver, so a released view is only noticed once something else starts frames. Until then the handle stays .paused/.running and finished() waiters stay suspended. Fix idea: notify on view deallocation (e.g. an associated-object sentinel whose deinit calls refreshDriver or cancels) instead of polling per frame.
close_reason: Views now carry an associated-object observer that cancels their handles when deallocated, so idle (paused, group-paused, wait(.infinity)) timelines end .cancelled without needing a frame. 5 new tests (confirmed failing without the fix); full scripts/ci-local.sh passes. Commit bd9af92.

title: Colour animations keep the traits captured at start when appearance changes mid-animation
description: Since kinieta-bwf, colorLerp resolves source and target once, against the view's traits when the animation starts. If the user toggles dark mode (or a sheet changes appearance) during a colour animation, the intermediate frames stay on the old variants and snap to the new target's variant at progress 1. Consider re-resolving when view.traitCollection's userInterfaceStyle/contrast changes (e.g. cache per trait collection) or registerForTraitChanges.
close_reason: Colour interpolators re-resolve source and target when the view's traits change colour appearance (hasDifferentColorAppearance), for .background, .borderColor and .custom colours. Unit test flips overrideUserInterfaceStyle mid-animation. Full scripts/ci-local.sh passes (201 iOS tests).

title: A paused or wait(.infinity) timeline that is dropped stays in Engine.actions forever
description: After kinieta-kce the driver stops while every action is idle, so no frames are spent, but a handle that is paused (or waiting on .infinity) and then released keeps its SequenceAction, its queued ActionTypes and their completion blocks in Engine.actions for the life of the process. Consider dropping idle sequences whose handle and view are gone, or documenting that callers must cancel.
close_reason: Engine drops idle timelines whose handle is gone (paused, or wait(.infinity)); handle deinit schedules the sweep. Full scripts/ci-local.sh passes. Follow-up: kinieta-3dp.

title: LCH and HSB intermediates are clamped to sRGB, so Display P3 endpoints pop at the end
description:
Property.swift:133 clamps every LCH intermediate to 0...1 sRGB (RGBColor.clamped) and HSB uses UIColor(hue:saturation:brightness:), which is sRGB. For P3 endpoints (getRed returns extended-sRGB values outside 0...1) the in-between frames lose saturation and the final frame jumps to the true P3 target. The .rgb mode already keeps extended values.

Slice: keep extended-sRGB components through the LCH path (clamp only to the P3 gamut, or not at all since UIColor accepts extended values); tests with UIColor(displayP3Red:...) endpoints checking the midpoint is outside sRGB; a P3 snapshot; README 'Colour'.

close_reason: LCH/HSB/RGB frames clip to the smallest of sRGB and Display P3 holding both endpoints (ColorMath.Gamut); tests for P3 midpoint outside sRGB and no pop near the end in all modes; P3 midpoint snapshots; demo P3 swatch; README/CHANGELOG. title: Performance: cache preset Bézier tables and avoid O(n) queue operations
description:
- Every easeIn()/easeOut()/easeInOut()/easing(.in(...)) call builds a new Bezier, which bakes a 1,001-point table (Bezier.swift:59-68: ~16 KB allocation and 1,001 polynomial evaluations). Building timelines in a list or a repeat loop pays this per call. README says curves are baked 'once', which is only true per instance.
- ActionQueue.popFirstAction uses removeFirst (O(n)) and popAllUngrouped inserts at 0 (O(n²) overall for long chains / large repeat counts).
- Engine.remove uses firstIndex (O(n) per finished action).

Slice: static cached presets (21 lets); index-based queue or Deque; measured with a performance test (XCTest measure or a Swift Testing timed loop) before/after.
acceptance_criteria: Performance test shows preset easing lookup allocates no new table; a 10,000-action timeline builds and runs in linear time.
notes: Done in 216eb4c. Presets are static lets in Easing.Preset; ActionQueue is index-based and holds the timeline (Kinieta.timeline reads mainSequence.queue.steps); Engine.update removes finished actions in one pass (first entry only, see handleExtendedInTheFrameItFinishedKeepsRunning). Tests/KinietaTests/PerformanceTests.swift: preset table sharing (buffer identity) plus 2,500 vs 10,000 scaling checks (fail above 8x). 10k eased steps, debug sim: 3.30 s -> 0.88 s (presets) -> 0.07 s. Full scripts/ci-local.sh passed.
close_reason: Presets cached, queue index-based, engine removes finished actions in one pass; perf tests added; full local CI passes.

title: API ergonomics: side-effecting 'then' property and ambiguous Easing.Curve.custom
description:
1. Kinieta.swift:85 `public var then: Kinieta` mutates the timeline in a getter: reading it twice (or in the debugger / a print) changes behaviour, and it cannot carry @discardableResult. A method then() reads the same and is honest.
2. Easing.Curve.custom(Bezier) plus Easing.custom(_:) duplicate each other, and Easing.in(.custom(b)), .out(.custom(b)), .inOut(.custom(b)) all ignore the placement silently (Easing.swift:52).

Slice: add then() and deprecate the property; deprecate Curve.custom in favour of Easing.custom (or document that placement is ignored); update README, DocC, demo and tests.
acceptance_criteria: Deprecated forms still compile with warnings; README/DocC show then() and Easing.custom only.
close_reason: then() added, then property and Easing.Curve.custom deprecated (compile with warnings); README, DocC, CHANGELOG and tests updated. Full scripts/ci-local.sh passed. Commit a4ab00e.

title: Warn in debug builds when a chain call is silently ignored
description:
Several builder calls quietly do nothing: easing after wait/parallel/group (Kinieta.swift:115-133, only the last animation is eased), delay/onComplete/easing on an empty timeline (popLast returns nil), then/parallel with nothing to gather, repeat(times: 0 or negative). title: macOS: follow the animated view's display, handle no screen
description: Engine.DisplayLinkDriver on AppKit takes its CADisplayLink from NSScreen.main (or the first screen), since the engine is shared by every view and NSView.displayLink suspends while the view is off screen. Consequences: a view on a second display with another refresh rate animates at the main screen's cadence (still on schedule, by elapsed time), and with no screen at all start() logs a warning and nothing animates, so completion blocks and finished() never return. Options: re-create the link when NSScreen.main changes (NSApplication.didChangeScreenParametersNotification / window screen changes), take the link from the screen of a running animation's view, and fall back to a Timer-driven clock when there is no screen.
close_reason: Display link follows the latest animated view's window screen (and moves on window/screen changes); a timer drives the engine with no screen. Full scripts/ci-local.sh passes.

Decide whether .x/.y keep frame-origin semantics once rotation exists (UIKit uses center/bounds so they survive a rotation).

title: Members stall behind a released group's infinite delay
description: Kinieta.group(a).delay(.infinity), with the group handle then released: the group's timeline waits forever and is dropped as abandoned, so member a reports .running but never starts, and its finished() returns only on a.cancel(). kinieta-3dp handed members back to the engine only when the group was paused. This case matches the wait(.infinity) contract ('waits until cancelled'), and a stays cancellable, so it may be intended. Options: leave it and document it, or hand the members back here too, which would start them without the delay.
close_reason: Chose 'leave it and document it': a member behind a released group's delay(.infinity) waits until cancelled on its own handle, matching wait(.infinity); handing it back would skip the delay. Documented in Kinieta.group docs and README; test aMemberBehindAReleasedGroupsInfiniteDelayWaitsUntilCancelled. Full scripts/ci-local.sh passes. Commit ee8e696.

title: Engine.remove is still a linear search for cancel and group
description: kinieta-4fu batched the removals of finished actions in Engine.update, but Engine.remove (used by Kinieta.cancel and Kinieta.group) still does firstIndex + remove(at:), so grouping k timelines while n are running costs O(k·n). Measured negligible at 10,000 timelines; only worth doing if grouping or cancelling very many timelines at once shows up in a profile.
close_reason: Engine.remove takes a batch in one pass; group and group cancel use it. 10k grouped+cancelled while 10k run: 43 s -> 0.23 s (debug sim). Scaling test added; full scripts/ci-local.sh passed. Done in 79315ed. A single cancel() is still O(n), as before.
